title: Citing Medicine, 2nd edition: Vancouver references (citation-sequence)
source: Karen Patrias, author; Dan Wendling, technical editor. Citing Medicine: The NLM Style Guide for Authors, Editors, and Publishers, 2nd edition, National Library of Medicine (US), 2007-, chapters 1 (journals) and 2 (books); and NLM, Samples of Formatted References for Authors of Journal Articles, https://www.nlm.nih.gov/bsd/uniform_requirements.html, read 2026-10-09. The CSL vancouver.csl (CC BY-SA 3.0) was read to learn the forms; nothing of it is copied.

rules.text: Sources are numbered in the order the text first cites them, starting at 1.
rules.source: Citing Medicine, introduction: the citation-sequence system

rules.text: The reference list runs in number order, one entry per number, with no gaps.
Every entry is cited in the text and every number cited has an entry.
A source cited again keeps the number it was first given; it is listed once.
Authors are written surname first, then up to the initials with no full stops or spaces between them, separated by commas.
With more than six authors, list the first six and then et al.; with six or fewer, list them all.
Journal titles are abbreviated as in the NLM Catalog, written without full stops.
A journal entry gives the date, then volume, issue and pages as year;volume(issue):pages, with no vol., no. or pp. and no spaces.
rules.source: Chapter 1A, date, volume, issue and location; NLM sample references, item 1

rules.text: A source read on the Internet carries [Internet] after the journal or title, the date it was cited in square brackets, and Available from: with its URL.
Article titles keep the capitals of the source in sentence form, no quotation marks and no italics.
An organisation as author is written in full as it appears on the source.
rules.source: Chapter 1A, author; NLM sample references, item 2

rules.text: A book entry gives the edition when it is not the first, then the place, the publisher and the year: 2nd ed. City: Publisher; 2022.
No detail the source does not give is added: an issue, a page range, a DOI or an access date is written only when it is known.
rules.source: Citing Medicine, general rules on what to include
